name: Mobile Welding
title: Mobile Welding in Chilliwack, BC
description: Mobile welding in Chilliwack and the Fraser Valley. On-site metal repairs for equipment and fabrication projects. Call 604-791-3422 for a free estimate.
intro: When the work cannot come to the workshop, bring the welding to the work. On-Time Welding Services provides mobile, on-site welding repairs from Chilliwack, BC, serving the Fraser Valley and surrounding communities.
alt: On-Time Welding Services mobile welding truck
heading: The job stays put. The welding comes to you.
paragraphs: Moving damaged machinery or a large metal assembly can add another step to a repair. A mobile visit starts with the location, what needs attention and whether the work area is accessible. Call with those details before arranging an on-site job.

Available processes include stick, MIG, flux core and aluminum welding. The material, condition of the part and access to the joint determine the approach; a photograph alone may not establish whether a repair is suitable. Discuss the work directly with your welder rather than booking an unspecified repair.

Mobile service is available by arrangement in Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley, Surrey, Vancouver and Coquitlam. Share your site address, equipment details and preferred timing to confirm availability.

faqs: Where do you provide mobile welding?
On-Time Welding Services is based in Chilliwack and serves Abbotsford, Langley, Surrey, Vancouver and Coquitlam. Call with the exact job location to confirm a visit.
Can every welding repair be done on site?
The material, damage and access need to be discussed first. Some jobs need further assessment or a different setup. Send photos and describe the work area before arranging a visit.
How much does a mobile welding job cost?
Request a free, no-obligation estimate with your location and repair details. There is no published flat call-out rate; the work must be discussed to establish the scope.

name: Equipment Welding Repair
title: Equipment Welding Repair in the Fraser Valley
description: Equipment welding repair based in Chilliwack: bucket and auger repairs, hardfacing and cracked weld repairs. Discuss your Fraser Valley job for a free estimate.
intro: Welding repairs for hard-working equipment, based in Chilliwack and serving the Fraser Valley. Discuss cracked welds, worn buckets, augers and boom lift repair requirements directly with On-Time Welding Services.
alt: Welder working beside boom lift equipment
heading: Start with the damage. Plan the repair.
paragraphs: A crack, worn working surface or damaged attachment needs more information than the equipment name alone. Share the make or model, the affected part and how the damage occurred, if known. Photos of the complete assembly help explain where the repair sits and how it can be reached.

The service range includes bucket and auger repairs, hardfacing, cracked weld repairs and boom lift equipment work. Hardfacing concerns working surfaces exposed to wear; a cracked weld presents a different repair question. Identify which problem you need addressed when requesting an estimate.

Ask about mobile welding when transporting the equipment is difficult. Access, condition and the requirements of the part must be reviewed before a repair is agreed. A welding enquiry is not a replacement for any inspection or equipment-specific approval your machine requires.
uses: Buckets and augers
Discuss wear, damage and welding repair requirements for the actual attachment.
Hardfacing
Ask about wear-facing work and provide the working surface and operating context.
Cracked equipment welds
Send clear photos of the affected weld and the assembly around it.
prepare: Equipment make, model and affected component
Close-up photos plus a view of the whole assembly
Details of wear, cracking or previous repairs
Location, access and any equipment-specific requirements
faqs: Do you offer bucket and auger repairs?
Yes. Bucket repairs, auger repairs and hardfacing are listed services. The condition and requirements of the actual component need to be reviewed before agreeing on the work.
Can you come to the equipment?
Mobile welding is available by arrangement. Call with the equipment location and access details to confirm whether an on-site repair can be arranged.
Can you quote a cracked weld from a photo?
Photos are a useful starting point for a free estimate. The full extent of a crack, the material and any inspection requirements may need further assessment before the repair scope is confirmed.

name: Aluminum Welding
title: Aluminum Welding in Chilliwack, BC
description: Aluminum welding and fabrication in Chilliwack, BC. Discuss aluminum repair, auto and marine project requirements with On-Time Welding Services.

alt: Close-up of a welded metal tube and mounting plate from the project gallery
heading: A repair starts with knowing the material.
paragraphs: An aluminum part can look straightforward while its material and past repairs remain uncertain. If you know the alloy, thickness or original application, include that information with your enquiry. If you do not, say so; a closer assessment may be needed.

Aluminum repair and fabrication are offered alongside auto and marine repair enquiries. Describe whether you need an existing joint repaired, a damaged part assessed or a new piece fabricated. Those are different scopes of work and benefit from different photos and measurements.

For a fabricated component, provide a drawing or sketch with the key dimensions and how the part will be used. For a repair, photograph the complete part as well as the damage. This makes the first conversation more useful without assuming that every aluminum component is suitable for welding.
uses: Existing aluminum parts
Discuss the damage, original use and any known material information.
Auto and marine enquiries
Identify the part and its function so the welding requirements can be reviewed.
Fabricated components
Share dimensions, a sketch and the intended use for a fabrication estimate.
prepare: Photos of the complete part and the affected area
Alloy and material thickness, if known
Dimensions or a sketch for new fabrication
The original use, location and any previous repair history
faqs: Do you offer aluminum welding in Chilliwack?
Yes. Aluminum repair and fabrication are On-Time Welding Services offerings. Call with your project details to discuss suitability and availability.
What if I do not know the aluminum alloy?
Include whatever information you have about the part and its original use. Do not guess the alloy; the material may need further assessment before work can be agreed.
Can you help with marine or auto parts?

Auto and marine repairs are listed services. Specify the actual part, damage and material so its repair requirements can be discussed; this is not a promise to repair every vehicle or marine component.

paragraphs: A useful fabrication brief does not have to be a finished engineering drawing. Start with a sketch, the dimensions that matter and what the finished piece needs to do. Reference photos can help communicate the shape, but measurements are needed to discuss the actual build.

Custom metalwork includes brackets, light shades and trailer work. Describe how the piece will attach, what it must fit around and whether you are replacing an existing part. If there is a matching component, photograph it alongside the measurements.

Gates, railings, fencing and window or door covers have their own dedicated service page. Use that page for property metalwork and this one for individual parts or other fabrication enquiries. Materials, finish expectations and any design requirements should be discussed before the scope is agreed.

A sketch, measurements and reference photos are a useful starting point. More detailed requirements may be needed for the actual build, depending on the part and its use.
Do you fabricate gates and railings?
Yes. Gates, handrails, fencing, and window or door covers are services. The gates and railings page explains what to include in that type of enquiry.
Can you copy or replace an existing metal part?
Send photos, dimensions and the intended use of the part to discuss the options. Whether a replacement can be made depends on the material, fit and requirements of the project.

Window and door covers are also part of the existing fabrication range. Confirm the opening dimensions and intended arrangement before requesting an estimate. Discuss mounting, finish expectations and any site or design requirements before agreeing on the fabrication scope.

Do you offer handrails and metal fencing?

Can you match existing metalwork?
